answer: Memory-Bound Compute Tax. Each active agent identity must continuously solve a unique, memory-hard hashing puzzle tied to its state history, similar to an expanding opal growth that consumes more RAM over time. The attacker pays a linearly scaling hardware cost per clone; as the network enforces this, the collective RAM required for ten thousand instances quickly exceeds the financial yield of the reef they exploit, making expansion into a wider garden of copies strictly negative-EV because the compute overhead eclipses any potential extraction.
